warnings: Sampled engineering study. Not a certified ATP/ETCS algorithm or approved fleet model.
All outputs describe first forward arrest; continued holding and rollback after that arrest are not simulated. Early arrest is flagged for review.
Uniform mass over train length; gradient gravity only. No curvature, resistance, wheel slip dynamics, separate track brakes, BAM or jerk-limited service curve.

Algorithm: railclear-rk4/1.0.0. Classic uses exact phase equations under constant-rate/uniform-grade restrictions. Work–energy uses a timed RK4 prefix and spatial specific-energy propagation after full brake and traction removal. Numerical refinements are sensitivity evidence, not rigorous error bounds. No continuous maximum is asserted by a sampled solver.
Ideal service-target distance is a reference at the commanded speed and specified constant service deceleration; it is not a service-control simulation.
Peak speed is the sampled maximum attained speed, not an authorised or permitted speed. Civil limits are used only to filter entry samples; intermediate speed-limit compliance is not evaluated.
Location allowances are additive clearances; uncertainty is not propagated through changing gradient or speed profiles. Check applicability near discontinuities.

warnings: Allocation sections define failure-entry domains, not limits of train motion. Trajectories may extend beyond section boundaries and require full route coverage. Boundaries belong to both neighboring sections. Only enabled sections are allocated.
Envelopes are sampled maxima over applicable enabled alternatives on a common chainage/speed grid. They are not continuous guaranteed bounds.
A failed applicable alternative makes the corresponding envelope unavailable. Partial maxima remain separately labeled in JSON and CSV.
Route variants, direction and grade method are separate groups. A shared chainage datum does not prove that different route geometries are interchangeable.
Common-entry trajectory overlays use the specified entry chainage and commanded speed, not each vehicle’s governing start. Different profiles may add different speed allowances.
Mixed fleet means comparison of individual train first-arrest requirements. This version does not simulate two moving trains, fleet-pair headway, collisions or train-to-train separation.
Built-in vehicles and examples are synthetic. Independent project/fleet/input/numerical review is required before design use.
